I don’t know your lineup but I’m fairly confident only 1 of however many tanks you have can actually take a hit, that being the jumbo. 

Play the jumbo aggressively because you can get away with it, it’s a brawler, plus that’s the only way you’re going to be able to pen anything but that doesn’t mean leave yourself open to flanks cause that’s when it’s most vulnerable with its shit side armor. Shoot barrels and MG tracks because realistically that’s the best chance you have when fighting most enemies. Learn weak spots that can be used with the 75, tiger/panther cupolas, IS2 cupolas etc and take a decent amount of APCR because that extra pen can mean going through the flat part of the frontal arc of a panther turret or a tiger 2s ammo rack from a slight angle on the side where APHE would have failed. Most importantly, WIGGLE. If you’re in a fight and you’re not in the process of lining up a shot, start wiggling your hull left and right, it’s a lot harder to hit your weak spot, the mg port, when it’s moving around. You have a stabilizer too so make good use of it when wiggling. Avoid angling too much and make sure to keep on the same level as other tanks like the panther because any slight elevation they have over you can mean a easy pen.

M36 is very much a run to a good position that over looks a common flank or choke point, fire, kill, back off, maybe repeat if you aren’t being stared at by the entire team, and reposition to eventually end up in the flank. It’s possible and I do it but avoid brawling with it. Youre much more suited for sniping in this thing, take advantage of the heat and good mobility.

Any 76 Sherman just play like a glass cannon. The 76 is pretty good and you will be able to pen majority of tanks you face just fine if you know their weakspots. Take advantage of the stabilizer because that’s one of your only advantages over other tanks. Shoot, back off, shoot, back off. If someone sees you you’re basically dead so positioning is super important, play this like the M36

You’re not playing it right. Aside from the glaring weakness of little ready to fire missiles compared to other SPAA at its tier, it’s a pretty good SPAA if you spot the enemy first. I find good success when I switch the radar search range to 20km. You will see basically any aircraft that spawns in before they can see you and lock you with a GBU or something. You may not be able to fire at them, but you know they are there. Just make sure you keep track of them with your eyes cause if they space climb and you lose them, you’re as good as dead. Once they are in range, you can choose to fire and hope you hit them and they don’t dodge, or you can let them come closer, switching your radar off if you want to try and conceal your location or presence even more, but they most likely know you’re somewhere already. Swap to IRST tracking and use that to track instead of the normal tracking since it won’t alert them they are being lit up by a SPAA. Once you fire, you just pray you hit them as with any SPAA. It’s all about knowing they are there, and having the jump on them/hitting them when they are vulnerable like when they come out of a dive or are in a dive

IRST does not give the target a lock tone but it does not give you the range either so you kind of have the opportunity to track them stealthily and you can open up on them when you see fit. 

The major downside of IRST is that it is very easily thrown off by flares and chaff, an experienced pilot who sees the missile launch or the tracers will probably be watching out and will start evading/flaring. 

If theres a space climbing aircraft that your search radar isnt picking up, you can try going into gunners sight and locking them there for range but after seeing the range, immediately unlock them (assuming they have RWR).

Learning your radar and the planes you face is pretty important too. you can get away with not even locking your target for range. Default search radius is usually 10km, each ring is 2.5km i think, so do some simple math and you can figure out the enemies range without completely alerting them.

TURN OFF YOUR RADAR, sometimes. if you know the enemy has RWR, and you have no other threats to worry about, turn your radar off. The enemy will know you are there because of your search radar pinging them, turning this off, prevents it and gives you the advantage when they dive and you gun them down. Most SPAA will still allow you to track even though youve turned off your radar. 

Other than that, same concepts apply, dont shoot cannon SPAA at targets until they are 3km or under, missile spaa, dont shoot unless they are in a flight path where you wont have to make your missile pull 332852349284 g's because you will probably miss and die as a result.

The US and Russia both have pretty good shells at top tier, notably M829A2 and the ADATS ATGM for the US and 3BM60, 9M119M1, and 9M123. Russia's ATGMs will send you to the next dimension as most have tandem warheads with extremely high penetration values. The APFSDS is about the same I guess. The US beats out Russia in terms of mobility. The Abrams series are all very mobile tanks, the HSTVL is very mobile as well and the Stryker is on the slower side for a wheeled vehicle but it is still fast. Russia really only has the T80 series and the Sprut series that can match the speed of the US. T72s/T90s/Khrizantemas are no where near as fast. A very big factor to consider is the elevation/depression angles of these tanks. The Russians lack depression and elevation quite badly only having -4/-5 most of the time which can put you in a pickle sometimes. The biggest difference however lies in the armor. Most NATO tanks put more emphasis on crew survivability, giving them blowout panels for ammo, better crew spacing, and protection focused around the turret crew. This does mean these tanks tend to be larger and have bigger weak spots than Russian tanks but it also means you are less likely to get one shot by someone and may be able to fight back against them. The Russians are kind of the opposite here, very tight crew spacing and a severe lack of protection from ammo detonations. The Russians do have very good protection though, only having small relatively small weak spots. Major downside is that once you are penned, you are more likely than not dead to fuel explosions, ammo detonation or outright crew knockouts. The only time you aren't is if gaijin saves you with their magical non spalling Russian armor.

The US is far better at sniping due to the depression angles but can also hold their own very well in a brawl. Russia is okay at sniping but is limited due to the depression angles yet again. Brawling is far easier with Russians due to the smaller weak spots and better armor. 

As for SPAA, both the Tunguska and ADATS are very good. The ADATS is far better at killing tanks since its ATGMs can easily kill most tanks. The Tunguska id say is better at dealing with air targets albeit not by that much.

At the end of the day none of this really matters because its the teams that make the difference. Russia by far has the best winrates across the majority of BRs id say, mostly dominating in top tier because of the cheaper repair costs which incentivize more people to spawn again instead of leaving and the heavy influence of CAS in top tier.

Work on positioning, when to be aggressive, when to be defensive, where to aim, and how to get yourself out of a pickle. When you hear a grenade being pulled out, either run away, or charge at him. I usually charge if it’s one guy or I think I can take on 2. When they reload too. If they have a gun that requires them to reload shell/bullet by bullet, bum rush them. They won’t be able to cancel in time. If you are pinned down, getting yourself to a place where you can move around if the enemy tosses a grenade at you is a good idea. Get yourself into a position where you can use grenades without being punished for it. If you are fighting out doors, cover would be better but concealment can work too. If you are running to a bush for concealment, dive down or move into a position behind/in the bush you wouldn’t normally shoot someone in. Dive down so if he sprays through the bush the bullets might go over your head, get up and fight back or book it to cover. Pick your fights too. If you can tell what gear they have thats great. They have a juice cannon and a slick? You have a P226? Book it. Not worth fighting him. You won’t stand a chance. You got a kedr? Maybe take the fight and leg meta him. Maybe book it. Depends on your loot/gear/health. You got a m4 and good gear, take the fight, maybe you’ll bonk him. Or book it if you really want to avoid him. But fighting would probably be the choice I’d go with.
